name: Sam
text:
Gemini 4 Hydrogen just built a horse out of Minecraft blocks and called it a day 

Same prompt, 4 AI workflows: a horse galloping through water.

Same horse, same lake, but the gap between the results is brutal 

The horse racing department is cooked

🥇 Fable 5.2 → low-poly horse in a low-poly world, huge water splashes and a gallop that actually looks heavy

🥈 Gemini 4 Carbon → warm sunset canyon, smooth horse and a very cinematic look

🥉 GPT-6 Astra → beautiful mountains and forest, but a low-poly horse inside a realistic world

💀 Gemini 4 Hydrogen → somehow a black voxel horse that looks like it escaped from Minecraft

The interesting part isn’t the horse

It’s how the legs, the splashes and the reflections work together

Pretty lighting can’t save you if the water doesn’t react to every hoof

Fable made the whole scene feel like one world, while Astra’s horse and background look like they belong to different games

At this point AI doesn’t need better horses

It needs to learn how water works 

Which horse would you pick?

在并发、异步、随时可能中断的真实环境里

followup → send → wakeDriver → kick

text:
Tidewater Abbey

Antigravity 
Gemini Neon High
 /Swarm 

Boxes
101.3 million boxes in the final build, each one placed and lit in the browser.
That is a third more than Eclipse Village (75.9 million).

Voxels (the 3D grid the light is ray traced through)
71.4 million cells at 22 cm, covering a world about 104 m wide and 70 m tall.
7.2 million cells are filled.
About 2,387 light sources: lanterns, lamps and lit windows.

Tokens (Gemini 4 Neon High)
153 million tokens in total.
134 million input: 82 million fresh and 52 million read from cache.
18.7 million output, of which 6.3 million are thinking.
1,510 model calls across 200 agent conversations.

Code
204 modules: 100 district tiles, 100 detail modules and 4 base modules.
25.3 MB of generated JavaScript, about 527,000 lines.

The film build is one HTML file of 26 MB.
The film
2 minutes, 4K, 24 fps, 2,880 frames in 12 shots.
Ray traced at 10 samples per pixel, about 239 billion samples.
12.4 hours of rendering on one Mac GPU, including the 2.5-hour fix pass. Frames average 12.5 seconds.
